verdict: Cincinnati Financial's revenue fell 18% to $3,047M because investment gains collapsed from $853M to $20M, even though premiums grew 5% and underwriting stayed profitable.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: $3,047M vs $3,726M a year ago — the drop is investment gains, not insurance

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: diluted, vs $7.11 a year ago; non-GAAP operating EPS was $2.86, flat vs $2.85

kpis.label: P&C combined ratio
kpis.note: claims plus expenses as a share of premiums — below 100% means underwriting made money; it was 88.2% a year ago

segments.name: Property casualty premiums
segments.note: Premiums earned on property and casualty policies — commercial lines $1,270M, personal lines $888M, excess and surplus lines $187M and other (reinsurance and global specialty) $260M. Up about 5%.

segments.name: Life insurance premiums
segments.note: Premiums earned by the life insurance subsidiary, mainly term life. Up 2%.

segments.name: Net investment income
segments.note: Interest and dividends earned on the investment portfolio, net of expenses — up 10%, with bond interest up 11%.

segments.name: Investment gains and other
segments.note: Net investment gains of $20M plus $12M of other revenues. A year ago investment gains alone were $853M — the swing explains the whole revenue drop.

opex.name: Underwriting and insurance expenses
opex.note: The cost of selling, underwriting and administering policies — commissions, salaries and operations.

opex.name: Other operating expenses
opex.note: Other operating expenses outside insurance underwriting.

otherDetail: Other expense is $12M of interest expense on the company's debt.
oneTimers: Investment gains and losses swing this company's reported profit: net investment gains were just $20M this quarter vs $853M a year ago. Excluding them after tax, non-GAAP operating income was $443M — essentially flat vs $449M a year ago — even though GAAP net income fell 59%.

Catastrophe losses were heavier than a year ago, adding about 7 points to the property casualty combined ratio versus last year's third quarter, which the company noted was closer to a historical third-quarter average.
footerNote: For an insurer, the direct-cost block here is insurance losses and contract holders' benefits — the claims paid and benefits owed. Investment gains and losses are counted in revenue, exactly as Cincinnati reports them. Figures are rounded to $M.

takeaways.title: Profit fell on investments, not insurance
takeaways.text: Net income fell to $459M from $1,122M, almost entirely because net investment gains dropped from $853M to $20M. On the company's non-GAAP operating view, which strips those gains out, income was $443M vs $449M — flat.

takeaways.title: Underwriting stayed profitable
takeaways.text: The property casualty combined ratio was 90.9% — for every $100 of premiums, about $91 went to claims and expenses, leaving an underwriting profit. It rose from 88.2% a year ago because catastrophe losses were about 7 points heavier.

takeaways.title: Premiums and investment income grew
takeaways.text: Earned premiums rose 5% to $2,690M, with property casualty net written premiums up 2% in the quarter on price increases and more insured exposures. Pretax investment income rose 10% to $325M, and book value per share was $105.42.
